description:
## Question

We need a server speaking the Bazel remote-execution API (the API buck2 uses) that can run on every developer machine, darwin and Linux, as a per-user service. Survey NativeLink, bazel-remote, buildbarn, BuildBuddy and anything else credible. For each:

1. Can it run as a **cache only** (action cache + CAS, no workers)? Can it run **with local workers** that execute actions on the same machine? Do those workers work on darwin?
2. Has it been used with buck2 (buck2 docs, `examples/remote_execution/` in the buck2 repo)? What `[buck2_re_client]` configuration does it need?
3. Packaging in nixpkgs (package name and version), footprint (memory, disk, startup), storage limits and eviction.
4. Sandboxing and hermeticity on workers: are only declared inputs visible to an action?
5. Can the same server later be pointed at, or replaced by, a shared remote-execution backend without changing cache keys?

comments.text:
Resolution. Findings are in docs/research/local-re-api-servers.md on local jj bookmark research/re-servers-local (commit e94112597afe; workspace turnkey-research-re-servers-local). This was desk research only; no server was run. buck2 citations are at HEAD b8ae22e6.

- Local WORKERS that run natively on darwin: only NativeLink and Buildbarn.
  - NativeLink: single process, but FSL-1.1 (source-available), not in nixpkgs, darwin barely CI-tested.
  - Buildbarn: 4-5 processes, and its scheduler ignores buck2's platform properties (buck2 sends them only on the deprecated Command.platform; PR #1366 is open). Workaround: an empty worker platform (untested).
  - BuildBuddy: its executor needs an enterprise licence.
  - buildbox-casd: local execution on macOS unconfirmed.
- CACHE-ONLY: bazel-remote fits best. It's in nixpkgs (darwin and Linux), a single binary, has a size-capped LRU, validates that cache hits' outputs exist by default (avoids buck2#862 dangling-hit failures), and can gRPC-proxy to a shared backend.
- buck2 client constraints: TCP only (no unix sockets; one loopback port per user), tls must be set false, engine_address required even for cache-only (must answer GetCapabilities), use SHA256.
- Isolation: no candidate sandboxes on darwin. Workers stage only declared inputs and clear env, but /nix/store and $HOME stay readable.
- Cache-only caveat: local build actions run in the repo root with the daemon env, so uploaded results can depend on unkeyed files and env.
- Swapping backends: buck2 computes the keys, so they're stable across backends if hash, platform properties, output-path mode and instance name match. bazel-remote proxy, NativeLink fast_slow, Buildbarn readCaching and casd --ac-remote can all front a shared store.
- Failures: NativeLink caches only exit 0; casd caches failures by default.
- Ruled out: justbuild (rejects buck2 uploads, Linux-only) and EngFlow single-node (proprietary Linux Docker).

title: Which remote-execution-API servers can run on a developer machine?
